t: #3565 Sequential Grid Path Cover — Backtracking over the Whole Grid
o: We must output a Hamiltonian path over all m*n cells (at most 25) that additionally visits the cells labeled 1..k in increasing order. Cells labeled 0 are free. Example 1 has a snake-like path through all 6 cells hitting 1 then 2 in order; Example 2 fails because the geometry forces 2 before 1. With at most 25 cells and 5x5 grids, exponential search with pruning is perfectly fine — no polynomial algorithm is needed.
k: The grid is tiny (≤ 25 cells), so DFS backtracking with pruning is the intended solution.
Prune aggressively: whenever we enter a cell whose label is neither 0 nor the next expected value, backtrack immediately.
Trying every starting cell covers all possible paths.

a.n: Approach 1: DFS Backtracking with Expected-Value Pruning
a.i: Do a plain Hamiltonian-path DFS, but carry the next required label `exp`. A cell with value v != 0 is enterable only if v == exp, in which case exp increases by 1; a 0-cell leaves exp unchanged. This prunes huge portions of the search tree, and since the grid has at most 25 cells the worst case is easily fast enough.
s: From every cell, DFS keeping a visited matrix and the path list.
On entering a cell, reject unless its value is 0 or equals the expected next label; advance the expectation when consumed.
When the path length reaches m*n, return it; otherwise backtrack. Return [] if no start succeeds.
a.t: Exponential in theory (Hamiltonian path), but at most 25 cells with strong pruning — instantaneous in practice.
a.sp: O(m*n) for the visited matrix, path, and recursion stack.

w: Backtracking is the only sensible tool here; do not look for a polynomial construction. Pitfalls: forgetting that a 0-cell does not advance the expected label, and forgetting to try all starting cells. Follow-ups: count all paths (return the count instead of one path), or handle larger grids where bitmask DP over rows (broken-profile DP) becomes necessary.
